Commentary.Commentary: Afghanistan now have more than 1 session to chase this down and they should back themselves to do so. The wicket is still a good one to bat on. Zimbabwe though have to take early wickets. They have got the 'hosts' bowled out for a low score twice in this series. Can they do it again?

The two continued their fight on the morning of Day 5. They added over 150 runs before Tiripano was dismissed in the 90s. Williams though continued, he got to the 150-run mark. Blessing did hang around for a bit but once he fell, the last wicket stand did not last for long.

It is Rashid Khan who leads his team off the field and rightly so! A superb bowling effort from him and have to say, it is only because of him, his side now has a big chance of levelling the series. However, a lot of credit has to be given to Zimbabwe for the character they have shown. Hats off to their skipper, who was absolutely sensational. Zimbabwe were down and out at 142 for 7 but Williams and Tiripano fought it out in the last session on Day 4.

OUT! LBW! The last wicket stand does not last for long! Rashid gets his 7th and his 11th in the game! The googly by him, it lands on off and then spins back in. Nyauchi looks to flick but misses. It hits the pad. They appeal and up goes the finger. ZIMBABWE BOWLED OUT FOR 365! THEY HAVE SET A TARGET OF 108!
Fullish and on middle, it's knocked down to long on for a run. Victor has two balls to survive.
Loopy and around leg, Sean sweeps it down to fine leg for two. 150 up for the Zimbabwean skipper!
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Floated and full on off, Williams reverse sweeps but finds point.
Victor Nyauchi is the new batsman.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! The dropped chance has not cost a lot. Hamza gets his man. Zimbabwe 9 down now. This is tossed up nicely, it lands on off and then spins away. Blessing defends inside the line. It takes the edge and goes into the gloves of the keeper. There is a huge shout and the finger goes up. The stand which was frustrating Afghanistan has been broken. Muzarabani is not happy with the decision and rightly so. The replays show there was a clear gap between bat and ball.
Floats it up, this time Muzarabani defends it.
On middle, this is whipped through mid-wicket for one.
On off, this is pushed to covers.

PUT DOWN! Ahmadi is the culprit! This could prove costly as this is one of the rare chances that has come Afghanistan's way. The plan almost worked. They had a man in the deep. Hamza tosses it up on middle. Blessing swings again. It goes off the inner half towards the deep mid-wicket fielder who moves to his right but spills it. A single taken.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Leans forward to a full ball on off and gently defends it to the cover region.
Rashid serves another flat delivery on off, it's on the shorter side again and Sean is on the back foot in defense.
Flatter and shorter on off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
FOUR! Lead crosses 100! Tossed up ball on middle, Williams goes down on one knee and sweeps it behind square leg. The call is for two but it has gone past the rope. Moves to 147!
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it watchfully.

FOUR! Four boundaries in the over! The lead is closing in on 100 now! At one stage that looked impossible. On middle, Blessing continues to go after the left-arm spinner. He once again hits it over mid-wicket for another boundary.
FOUR! And again! Third boundary in the over! Hamza continues to give it air. Muzarabani once again heaves it over the mid-wicket fielder for another boundary.
FOUR! Dragged again! This is floated up outside off, Blessing manages to play the sweep, it is hit through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Floats it up on middle, blocked.
Shorter and on middle, defended.
FOUR! Blessing says, enough of blocking. He plays a wild slog. Connects it well and manages to drag it from outside off over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Well played! This is shorter, it rises after landing. Williams does well as he plays it with soft hands on the off side.
That has spun sharply! It lands on off and then spins away. Williams goes back and tries to block but it goes past the bat by a long way.
On middle, sold defensive stroke again.
Close! The leg spinner, it lands outside off. Williams ends up defending outside the line. It hits the inside edge, then the pad and falls onto the ground.
Once again on the stumps, this is played back to the bowler.
Tossed up on middle, Williams defends it.
A maiden! On off, this is defended.
Almost! This lands on off and then spins away. Blessing looks to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge, hits the pad of the keeper and rolls on the off side. Lucky escape for Blessing.
Slightly shorter, turns a bit but Blessing has enough time to adjust and block.
Well left! Slower and outside off, BM watches it and lets it be.
Lovely delivery! This drifts in from outside off, it lands and then spins away. Blessing looks to defend but is beaten.
Tossed up outside off, Blessing has a poke at it but is beaten.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out. End of a testing over by Rashid.

Aerial but safe! Flatter and shorter on off, Williams hangs on the back foot to punch it through covers but it stops a bit onto him and takes the toe end of the bat. Loops in the air but doesn't carry to mid off.
A low full toss wide outside off, Williams reaches out and pushes it to point.
Floated and full on off, Sean prods forward and this time manages to defend it from the middle of his blade.
Beaten! A googly landing around off, Williams tries to defend but getting forward but it turns past his bat.
Quicker and fuller on middle, skidding off the surface, Williams lunges and blocks it solidly.
Floats it up on off, Blessing is solid in defense.
Another one on middle, kept out.
On middle, it is defended.
Angled into the pads, Blessing works it to mid-wicket.
Shorter and on off, Williams goes back and pushes it down to long on for one.
On middle, it is defended.
Blessing plays it well again! Tossed up on middle, it is defended nicely.
On middle, Williams looks to defend. It goes off the outer half through point for one.

FOUR BYES! Bonus runs for Zimbabwe! Williams looks to sweep, this lands outside off and then spins away. Also stays a touch low. Sneaks under the bat, goes past the keeper and the slip fielder for a boundary.
On the shorter side once again, Williams mistimes his cut to covers.
Lands outside off and turns back in. Defended.
Shorter and outside off, Williams slaps it towards cover where the fielder dives and stops it.
Shorter and around off, Blessing guides it to point.
Fuller and on middle, this is pushed back to the bowler.
Back of a length again and on off, it is played to point.
Good length and on middle, Blessing keeps it out.
Once again a little too short, pulled through square leg. Easily one.
Outside off, Williams looks to drive it on the off side but it goes back to the bowler off the inner half.
BEATEN! Two good balls to end! This is quite full and outside off, googly again, turns back in from outside off. Muzarabani is beaten as he tries to drive.
A huge, huge appeal but turned down! Going over maybe! This is a googly, it lands outside off and spins back in. Blessing goes back to flick but misses. He gets hit near the knee roll. Looked close.
Floats it up on middle, defended.
Shortish again, Blessing goes back and blocks it.
On middle, defended.
Edgy run! It lands on off and then it spins away. Williams looks to defend but it goes off the outer half towards point for one.
Another short one to end, ducked under with ease.
Good length and on middle, blocked.
Top edge but safe! Shirzad bends his back on this one, it bounces at a good height. Williams is in no control of the pull. It lands well short of fine leg though for one.
One more short one on the body, it is evaded.
Shorter and around off, Williams looks to pull but it comes slowly off the surface. It is mistimed to mid-wicket.
Outside off and on a length, it is left alone.
Sayed Shirzad to bowl from the other end!
And he does well! On middle, it is played to the man at mid on.
On the pads, BM misses the flick and is hit on the pads. An appeal but turned down. One more ball to negotiate in this over.
Well played! Tossed up on off, Blessing watches it and plays it onto the ground.
A little too short this time, it turns back in. Muzarabani has enough time to go back and push it back to the bowler.
Slips this one down the leg side, Blessing looks to flick but misses.
A single to get the second session underway! Tossed up on off, Williams looks to drive, it is the leg spinner and hence, it goes off the inner half through mid-wicket for one.
Welcome back for the afternoon session. The players are back on the field as well. As expected, Rashid Khan to start proceedings...
... DAY 5, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, the lead is now 72 runs and with Sean Williams still unbeaten, Zimbabwe would be hoping that he farms the strike and add more valuable runs with the tail. For Afghanistan, the task is simple now, pick the remaining two wickets quickly and chase down the target on a relatively good pitch to bat on. Will they succeed? Do join us at 1210 local (0810 GMT) for the afternoon session to find out.

Lunch will taste good to Afghanistan now as they have at least one end open to pick wickets and close the Zimbabwean innings quickly after the break. It was hard work for them in the morning as their spinners were blunted to a large extent by Williams and Tiripano. Sayed Shirzad was the standout bowler in the first hour as he bowled with a lot of intent and troubled Donald with his accurate bouncers.

64/1 in the morning session where 30 overs were bowled. Runs don't matter really at this stage for Afghanistan and they would be pleased to finally break the strong resistance of Sean Williams and Donald Tiripano. It was a heartbreak for Donald Tirpano who was trapped in front by Rashid Khan and missed out on his maiden Test hundred by just 5 runs. The African team continued to show great fight in the morning session and their overnight pair nearly played out the entire session once again.
Floated and full ball on middle, Muzarabani brings down a straight bat in defense. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 5!
Flighted and on off, Williams looks to go over the top but the connection is not too good. It goes over mid on and they cross.
Turning back in from around off, Williams blocks it from the back foot.
Lunges to a full ball and defends it back.
Floated and full on off, Williams reverse sweeps it to point.

A low full toss on off, Williams drives it back to the bowler. A half-stop by the bowler but Sean decides not to run. Afsar Zazai is into Sean's ears advising him then he should take a run as Blessing can handle.
Beaten! A floated leg spinner landing close to off, Blessing lunges to defend but it spins past his blade.
Shortish and on middle and leg, Muzarbani plays it down from the crease to short leg.
Quicker and on off, defended off the back foot.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Flatter googly and outside off, defended off the back foot.
Blessing Muzarabani is the new batsman.

OUT! Given lbw! Heartbreak for Tiripano. Rashid strikes and gets his 10 wickets in the match. A well-disguised wrong 'un by him, landing around off and spinning back in. Tiripano goes deep inside the crease to defend but it stays a touch low too and strikes him on the pads. They appeal and the finger goes up. End of a brilliant 187-run stand and Zimbabwe lead by 71 runs.
Loopy ball, well wide outside off, Williams strides forward with a big stretch and then leaves it alone.
Quicker one on the pads, eased down to mid on for a run. Moves to 95!
Once again Tiripano is on the front foot in defense.
Gets forward to a full ball and drives it back to the bowler.
Slower through the air, full and wide outside off, Tiripano hits it back to the bowler.
A full toss on off, Williams lofts it down to long on for one. 10 minutes to Lunch, can Donald get to his ton before that?
Loopy and on middle, Tiripano gets forward and closes the face of his bat slightly as he blocks it towards square leg.
Fires a full ball on middle, defended back to the bowler.
A googly landing full on off, Tiripano lunges and defends it off the inside edge to square leg.
Fuller and on off, Williams drives it towards the bowler who fails to pick it up and they cross.
Fullish and on off, quicker through the air, Williams defends it off his front foot.
A googly around middle and off, Williams sticks back and plays close to his body. He tries to defend and does so off the outer half to point.
Change of ends for Rashid Khan. 5/126 in his 54 overs so far.
Play and a miss! Short and wide outside off, Tiripano rocks back to punch it through the line but it stays low and beats his bat.
Arm ball on leg, skidding down, Tiripano clips it off his pads to short fine leg.
Too full in length outside off, Sean drives it from the toe end of his bat through mid off and rotates the strike.
A low full toss on the pads, it's eased wide of mid on for a single.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, going on with the arm, DT defends again.
Fuller and on off, it's defended back to the bowler.
Yet another full toss on off, Tiripano forces it to deepish mid off for one. Moves to 93!
Extra flight this time, it's a full toss on off, Williams pushes it to mid off and rushes to the other end. Th lead is now 65.
Loopy and full outside off, Sean presses well forward and defends it watchfully.
Goes flatter through the air around leg, Donald turns it to square leg and rotates the strike.
Turn and bounce, from around off, Donald feels for it inside the line and gets beaten.
Full and flighted on middle, Sean flicks it to mid-wicket. They wait for the fielder to make his dive and once he does that and makes only a half-stop, they cross.
Flatter and wider outside off, Tiripano hits it through the line but finds the cover fielder.
Skidding down the leg side, Donald pads it away.
That is punched off the back foot back towards the bowler.
Hangs on the back foot to a short ball and punches it to covers.
Tossed up ball on middle, clipped on the leg side towards mid-wicket.
Half shout for an lbw! Inside edge, possibly. Flatter and around leg, Tiripano goes back and tries to defend. He is struck on the pads but indeed is off the inside edge, as confirmed by the replays.
Shahidullah Kamal is into the attack now, replacing Rashid Khan.
Edged but safe! Full and flighted outside off, Williams tries to drive but goes hard at it. The ball skids away to gather the outside edge and goes to short third man.
A full toss on middle, Donald doesn't try to hit it hard and just pushes it wide of mid on for a run. Moves to 91!
Another delivery around leg, Tiripano nudges it down to fine leg and calls two, two, two...even three... He will get two.
Fires one down the leg side, Tiripano goes back to guard his stumps as he makes a leave.
Gets forward to a full ball and pushes it gently with the spin to covers.
Full and around leg, skidding down, Tiripano tries to defend but misses and is pinged on the pads.
A googly landing around leg and turning towards off, Williams watchfully defends it from the back foot.
Another back foot punch by Donald, this time towards mid off where the fielder is late to take off. They cross for a run.
Shortish and on off, Donald goes on the back foot and pushes it to covers.
Sprays a full ball down the leg side, DT lets it be.
Floated and wide outside off, it's well left by Donald.
Nicely tossed up delivery, full and wide outside off, Tiripano drives but finds the cover fielder.
Extra loop on this one as it lands full on middle, Williams flicks but picks out the mid-wicket fielder.
Tossed up ball on off, spinning in, Williams moves back and punches it towards the bowler.
Flatter and on middle, defended from the back foot to the leg side.
A touch short and on off, Tiripano goes back and hits it down to long on for a run. 50 runs have been accumulated this morning.
Loopy and full around leg, Donald is watchful as he defends it down with soft hands.
Floated and full ball on middle, Willams works it away in the gap at square leg for a run.
Asghar Afghan trying something different. He has tossed the ball up to Rahmat Shah. He has a fifer in ODIs.

Quicker and shorter on off, Tiripano prefers staying on the back foot as he keeps it out safely to the off side. Another over goes and Afghanistan's search for a breakthrough continues. The last wicket fell in the 64th over.
Flatter leg spinner on off, Tiripano is squared up a bit but does well to defend it safely from the back foot.
Fullish and outside off, a googly, DT is forward in defense.
A back foot punch this time as Donald strokes a shortish ball to mid off.
Flatter and shorter delivery, a leg spinner, Tiripano goes on the back foot as he blocks it down.
Fuller and on off, Donald drives but finds the cover fielder. He is 14 short of his maiden Test hundred.
Hurls in a floated full around off, Williams gets forward to meet the ball and jams it down there and then.
Short and outside off, Williams punches it from the back foot to covers but Shahidi does well to make a diving stop.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball on off and defends it to mid-wicket.
Floated and full on off, Williams brings out the paddle sweep and sends it down to fine leg for two.
Slow turn back into the batsman, Sean goes back and helps it to short mid-wicket.
Lunges to a full ball around off and defends it to the off side.

FOUR! Top edge! Loopy and full, down the leg side, Tiripano spots the opportunity to sweep but fails to control it. It flies off the top edge but goes safely down to fine leg. He moves to 86 and the stand is now 170, which is now a record for the 8th wicket for Zimbabwe.
Rashid comes from 'round the wicket and serves a length ball on the pads, Tiripano taps it down to short leg.
Shortish and on off, Donald defends it out from the inside half of his blade.
Loopy and full around off, Williams tries to play the off drive but it spins back in to take the inside edge. The ball rolls through mid-wicket and they cross. LEAD IS NOW 50!
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it past the bowler to mid off.
Spinning away from the batsman, flatter through the air, it's outside off, Williams stands back and withdraws his bat.
Slow again, full and outside off, Tiripano is on the front foot as he defends it with an angled bat towards point.
Slow loopy full ball close to off, Tiripano is on the front foot as he offers a dead bat in defense.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, Tirpano gets forward and defends.
FOUR! Another controlled reverse sweep from the bat of Tiripano. He picks the line to be around off, the length is also full and Donald forces it through point.
Tossed up ball landing full on off, Tiripano defends it back.
Quicker and flatter on off, fuller in length, Williams gets forward with a dead bat in defense.
A googly landing full outside off, Williams draws forward in defense and edges it past first slip. Two taken.
A bit short and outside off, Williams stands back and plays it towards point.
Quicker leg spinner on off, Williams goes on the back foot and blocks it safely to the off side.
Loopy and full on middle, Sean draws forward and defends it again.
Flighted and full around leg, Williams gets on the front foot and defends it to mid-wicket.
Floated and full on middle, Tiripano presses forward and defends it back with a straight bat.
Loopy and full on off, once again Donald plays the reverse sweep but finds backward point on this occasion.
Arm ball around middle, full and skidding down, Tiripano eases it off the inner half to short fine leg.

FOUR! Adventurous from Donald Tiripano. He brings out the reverse sweep and nails a full ball down to third man for a boundary. Moves to 78 and he will be eyeing his maiden Test hundred. 300 up for Zimbabwe, they lead by 43 runs.
Full and flighted on off, Tiripano gets forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Too full in length on middle, Williams knocks it down to long on and takes a single.

Drinks break. The first hour has been safely negotiated by the pair of Sean Williams and Donald Tiripano. They have stretched their lead and Afghanistan's frustration. Apart from an outside edge off Donald Tiripano not carrying to Rahmat Shah at first slip, there wasn't any notable moment in the first hour. So far so good from Zimbabwe and they would be hoping that the current pair bats for as long as possible and swell the lead to 100.
Floated and full on off, Tiripano is forward again in defense.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Loopy and full on middle, Tiripano defends it by getting forward.
Confident, very confident. Full and outside off, Donald drives it through the gap at covers for a couple of runs. The lead moves to 39.
Fires one down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone and Afsar collects it cleanly.
A tossed up ball on middle, turning down, Tiripano helps it off his pads to short fine leg.
FOUR! Slapped away! Short and wide outside off, Sean camps back and hammers it through covers for a boundary. The 150-run stand comes up!
Presses forward to a full ball and plays it with the spin to the on side.

Shout for a caught behind! Not given. A delivery landing full outside off and goes on with the arm, Williams tries to defend but it whizzes past the outside edge. Zazai collects, they appeal, unconvincingly though and the umpire shakes his head.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Short this time, outside off, Williams cuts it off his back foot to point.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and helps it with the spin to the leg side.
Change in bowling. Amir Hamza comes into the attack for the first time this morning. He's been wicket-less so far in the second innings.
A wrong 'un around middle and leg, Tiripano picks it as he works it to square leg. Another over safely negotiated and the lead has now moved to 32.
Quicker and flatter full ball on off, staying low, Donald does well to keep his eyes on the ball as he blocks it out.
FOUR! Down the ground from Tiripano! Slightly overpitched by Rashid Khan, it's outside off, Donald exercises his arms and smashes it over mid off for a boundary.
Loopy this time, full and around off, Tiripano gets forward and defends it to the off side.
Shortish and on off, Donald goes on the back foot and punches it down to mid on.
A flatter leg spinner on middle, not turning much, Tiripano helps it off his pads to square leg.
Way outside off, on a length, Williams is not going to chase it.
Fullish around leg, clipped towards square leg for a run.

DEAD BALL! Fuller in length and angling down the leg side, Tiripano shapes up for the flick shot but then pulls out. It goes off his pads past the keeper for a boundary but since there was no shot offered, four runs won't get added to Zimbabwe's total.
Short again, around off, Sean pulls it in front of square leg for a run. That's aerial for a moment.

FOUR! Bang! 1000 Test runs for Sean Williams! Short in length again, outside off, Williams fetches it from there and pulls it powerfully through the gap between mid on and mid-wicket. The lead moves to 26.
Short in length on middle, staying low, Williams tries to pull but fails to get hold of it.
No one in the catching position. Afghanistan have gone completely defensive. Maybe, they are offering an easy run to Sean Williams here, so that Shirzad can have a go at Donald Tiripano.
Strides forward to a full ball and pushes it to the off side, not in the gap again.
Full toss on middle, pushed down the ground but the mid on fielder makes the stop.

SAFE! Flighted and full landing close to off, Tiripano presses forward in defense but it spins away slightly to catch the outside edge. It goes behind towards first slip where Rahmat Shah bends to catch the ball. The keeper and the bowler set off in celebration but Rahmat is not too sure. The umpires get together before referring it upstairs. The soft signal remains not out and one replay is enough to suggest that the ball has bounced.
Has it been taken? The fielder in the slip cordon is not sure. Two umpires get together and take it upstairs. The soft signal is not out.
Flatter leg spinner on off, it's blocked off the back foot to covers.
Wrong 'un on the shorter side, Donald goes on the back foot as he defends it to the leg side.
Full and floated around middle, Tiripano gets on the front foot and defends it to the off side.
Fullish and outside off, Williams mistimes his off drive towards mid off.
Pitches it up and outside off, Williams drives it on the up but fails to beat the cover fielder.
Drifting down the leg side, Tiripano fails to work it around and it goes off his pads to fine leg for a leg bye.
A bouncer is followed by a fuller length ball, it's aimed at off stump and Donald gets forward to defend it back.
Sayed is putting Tiripano to the sword here. Digs in another bouncer on middle, Donald ducks at the last moment.
Back of a length ball on off, from 'round the wicket, Tiripano sticks back, keeps his eyes on the ball and defends it to the off side.
Flighted full ball on off, turning back in, Williams prods forward to defend and does so from the inside half of his bat. It falls short of short leg.
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it with soft hands to the off side.
Turn for Rashid but it takes the ball down the leg side, Williams tries to flick but misses.
A touch flatter and shorter on off, Williams goes on the back foot and defends it down towards the off side.
Loopy and full around off, Sean defends it from the middle of his blade this time.
Floated and full around off, Williams gets forward to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The Afghan players got excited for a while.

Physio comes out again! It's not been easy for Donald Tiripano this morning. Got one on the helmet earlier and now a painful blow on the body. Tiripano is lying on the ground as the physio is applying some ice on his back. Tiripano is finally back on his feet. Will these blows affect his concentration?

Hit on the body, they appeal for an lbw but Aleem Dar just quietly moves away. A bouncer around leg, Donald tries to duck but it doesn't rise much and brushes his left shoulder. They appeal but it's too high.
Spears in a full ball on middle, Donald gets forward and defends it back safely.
Shirzad goes short again but the angle of the delivery takes it down the leg side, Tiripano moves away from the line.
Short delivery again but this time the line is outside off, an easy leave for Donald.

Aerial but safe! Shirzad hurries up the batsman with a well-directed bouncer, Tiripano is very uncomfortable as he takes his eyes off the ball while fending it off. Gloves it but it falls safely towards point.
Sayed steams in from 'round the wicket and digs in a short ball around middle, Tiripano ducks underneath it.
Tossed up ball outside off, Williams lets that one go to the keeper.
A googly around off, Williams blocks it back solidly.
Turning down the leg side, Williams fails to flick and is hit on the pads, Rashid appeals but nothing from the umpire.
Flatter and shorter outside off, Williams punches it from the back foot to covers.
Loopy leg spinner landing outside off, Sean stretches his front leg forward to cover his stumps and spin before making a leave.
Flighted and full on middle, Williams flicks it off his front foot to short leg.
Sliding down the leg side from middle, Williams helps it off his pads to deep square leg and retains strike with a run.
Good length delivery outside off, staying low a bit, Williams watches it closely before making a leave.
Fuller in length and on off, Williams gets on the front foot and drives it back off the inner half of his bat.
A length ball close to off, attacking the stumps, Williams uses the angle and defends it towards mid on.
Solid in defense. Williams is on the front foot again, to a full ball and blocks it to the off side.
Full and on off, angling in, Williams blocks it off his front foot.
Floated and full outside off, Williams pushes it to covers where the fielder makes a half-stop. A dot to end the over!
Quicker and flatter outside off, Williams hangs back to punch it through the line but it takes the inner half of the bat and goes to the leg side.
Presses forward to a full ball and softly pushes it to covers.
Allows the ball to spin back into him and then helps it towards mid-wicket.
Loopy and full on off, Sean is on the front foot in defense.
Turning back in from around off, staying low, Williams does well to keep it out safely.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Well bowled! A terrific yorker around off, Tiripano does well to get his bat down in time as he digs it out to the off side.
Physio comes out! The mandatory concussion test is going on. All good!
Ouch! That's bang on the helmet. A bouncer around off, Donald take his eyes off the ball and gets hit on the helmet.
Pitches it up and outside off, Tiripano drives it through the line but finds the cover fielder.
Good length ball on off, defended from the back foot to point.
Beaten! Good length delivery outside off, Donald pushes inside the line and misses.
Shorter and on off, defended off the back foot. 6 from the over, the lead is now 19.
Nicely done, Williams is forward this time to a full ball and eases his drive in the gap at covers for a brace.
FOUR! Williams picks the short delivery early, goes back and allows it to spin back in before he whips it through mid-wicket.
Draws forward to a full ball and pushes it to mid off.
Drags his length short around off, Williams moves back and plays it down to mid-wicket.
Flighted and full outside off, Sean is on the front foot in defense.
Who will bowl from the other end? No prizes for guessing, it's Rashid Khan.
It's too full and outside off, Donald pushes it gently towards the cover fielder.
Fuller length ball close to off, it's been driven back in the direction of the bowler.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
FOUR! Angling away from the batsman, Tiripano has a push inside the line and gets an educated edge. It goes wide of the slip cordon for a boundary.
The length is full on this occasion, it has been worked towards square leg for a single.
AERIAL BUT SAFE! Back of a length ball angling in, Sean closes the face of the bat early and it loops just behind mid off.
Out come the players! Sean Williams and Donald Tiripano are in the middle as well. Sayed Shirzad to steam in first up...
Pitch report - It's slightly overcast at the moment but the sun will come out soon. The pitch is expected to behave the same as it was behaving on Day 4.

Yet another interview, this time it's of Regis Chakabva. Says that the pitch in the first Test had a little bit more grass and this one is bare. Mentions that there was some turn on Day 4. Tells that losing too many wickets wasn't ideal and they are looking forward to Williams and Tiripano taking them deep on the final day. Feels that it's going to be a good show of character from them. Adds that they just have to challenge themselves and if they get a lead close to 150 and leave very little time to Afghanistan, it would be interesting.

Afsar Zazai comes up for a quick chat! Says that today is a very important day and they have done well so far. Wants to pick the remaining wickets quickly and not allow Zimbabwe to put up a big total. Feels the pitch still looks good for batting. Mentions that after the first loss, they discussed in the dressing room and were hopeful of bouncing back strongly.

Afghanistan are still new in this format and are learning things the hard way. After enforcing the follow-on, they would have hoped to run through Zimbabwe in a jiffy but the current 8th wicket stand has proved to be a thorn in their flesh. The 'hosts' still hold the upper hand but they were made to work very hard in the last session of Day 4 that was wicketless. Some tired fingers of their spinners would have got a good night's rest and let's see whether they spin their magic this morning or not. Stay tuned for more as we approach the start...

We move into the final day of this Test series and it's hard to believe that Zimbabwe are still hanging in there, although by the skin of their teeth. Last evening we witnessed a lion-hearted effort by the pair of Sean Williams and Donald Tiripano as its unbeaten century stand not only put Zimbabwe in the lead but also stretched this Test match to Day 5. Their lead though is a slender one, let's see if they have more fight left in them to frustrate Afghanistan further.

The Afghans do not need to panic, they are still quite ahead in the game. However, they would want to pick up the three wickets quickly on Sunday because if this partnership just goes on for a while, they will start to worry. The visitors are ahead by 8 runs and will look to bat for longer and turn that lead into a hefty one. The first session on the 5th day could be an important one. Do join us at 0930 local (0530 GMT). Until then, cheers!

Sean Williams is the star for them with the bat with yet another ton for hm and even Tiripano has ended up playing a blinder. Zimbabwe will be hoping they can continue the good work on Day 5 and pull off a miracle.

PITCH REPORT - The cracks have started to open up and the balls hitting this area, are starting to misbehave more now. The batters for Zimbabwe looked good but they chased after deliveries, which they could have left and will look to do that better. It will be important to see how the Zimbabwean batters play against spin.

Sikander Raza is in for a chat now! He says that they have to take the time out of this day and they have to drag the game to Day 5. Says that their openers did really well but they did not back them up well and adds that he hopes that they can bat for longer. Feels that the conditions are slightly on the tricky side and the wicket had variable bounce as well and says that it was a good challenge.

Nasir Jamal is in for a quick chat! He says that he was really happy for his maiden Test fifty and he is feeling well. Says that it was a good partnership between Afghan and Shahidi and when he came to bat, it was slightly easier for him.

We head into Day 4 of the second Test between Afghanistan and Zimbabwe. The match only seems to be heading one way and that is an Afghan win. Zimbabwe are still 234 runs behind and their first aim will be to bat for as long, as possible. Their openers have started well but they need to keep going. Afghanistan, on the other hand, would love to finish this game today. Is it going to be the last day? We will find out soon enough.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

However, they would've loved a couple of wickets in these 13 overs of the second innings but that didn't happen. But they know that they have plenty of time left in this game. They will return on Day 4 fresh and look to take all the 10 wickets to level the series. For Zimbabwe, the task will be simple. Just keep batting. And that is not going to be easy on the 4th day deck. So, we are in for a cracking Day 4. The action will begin at 0930 local (0530 GMT). We will look for your company. For now, it is goodbye from our side. Cheers and take care.

The bowling from Zimbabwe was fine. They lacked discipline in the first session but managed a couple of wickets with Rashid and Hamza getting a wicket apiece. Shirzad returned and struck twice in two balls in the second session to thump Zimbabwe. Rashid then removed the set Musakanda. Burl didn't last long either as he was sent packing for nothing by Hamza. A few poor overs saw Afghanistan lose track towards the end of the second session. However, they did the rest in the last session to make sure they bundle Zimbabwe well before the follow-on score. Rashid was the pick of the bowlers as he got 4. Hamza did well for his 3. Overall, it was a decent bowling performance.

Earlier in the day, Zimbabwe did well in the first session. Their overnight batters played nicely. Kasuza was the first one to fall and his partner departed just before the Lunch break after going past his 3rd Test half-century. Skipper Williams failed to get going in this game as he got out cheaply in the second session. Madhevere fell for a first-ball duck and Zimbabwe lost the track a bit. Musakanda though went after Rashid and played a fine knock before falling to Rashid after getting into the 40s. Burl failed to open his account but Raza along with Chakabva counter-attacked and added 50 in quick time. Chakabva's knock was cut short when Zadran pouched a sharp chance at short leg, at the start of the evening session. Zimbabwe eventually rolled out for 287 with Raza playing a fine knock of 85 before getting out as the last man.

Zimbabwe have done well to see off these 13 overs. They did something similar on Day 2 as well. However, they know that they have a big, big task in front of them. And on the moving day of the Test, the game has certainly moved at a rapid pace. Afghanistan have plenty of runs for the cushion. The surface on Day 4 is eventually going to offer more assistance to their spinners which means at the end of Day 3, they are right on top.
